_comment: Canonical, beginner-facing definitions of Magic keyword abilities and common symbols. Passed to the model as authoritative reference so keyword explanations are grounded, not recalled from memory. Definitions are close to Wizards' official reminder text, simplified for new players. Keys are lowercase.
deathtouch: Any amount of damage this deals to a creature is enough to destroy it.
double strike: This creature deals combat damage twice: once with first-strike timing, then again at normal timing.
enchant: This Aura can only be attached to the kind of thing listed (for example 'enchant creature' means it goes on a creature).
equip: Pay the equip cost as a sorcery (only on your turn, when nothing else is happening) to attach this Equipment to a creature you control.
first strike: This creature deals its combat damage before creatures without first strike. If it kills the blocker/attacker first, that creature may never deal damage back.
flash: You can play this card any time you could cast an instant, including on other players' turns.
flying: This creature can only be blocked by creatures with flying or reach.
haste: This creature can attack and use tap abilities the same turn it comes under your control, ignoring the usual 'summoning sickness' wait.
hexproof: This permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.
indestructible: This can't be destroyed by damage or by effects that say 'destroy'.
lifelink: Whenever this deals damage, you gain that much life.
menace: This creature can't be blocked except by two or more creatures.
reach: This creature can block creatures with flying.
trample: When this creature attacks and is blocked, any leftover damage beyond what's needed to destroy the blockers can be assigned to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.
vigilance: Attacking doesn't cause this creature to tap, so it can still block on the next turn.
ward: Whenever this becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, that spell or ability is countered unless its controller pays the ward cost.
prowess: Whenever you cast a noncreature spell (instant or sorcery, usually), this creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.
scry: Look at the top card(s) of your library. You may put any of them on the bottom; the rest stay on top in any order you choose.
surveil: Look at the top card(s) of your library. You may put any of them into your graveyard; the rest stay on top in any order you choose.
fight: Two creatures each deal damage equal to their power to the other, at the same time.
mill: Put the top card(s) of a library into its owner's graveyard.
flashback: You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then it's exiled (removed from the game) instead of going back to the graveyard.
convoke: You can tap untapped creatures you control to help pay this spell's cost. Each creature pays for {1} or for one mana of its color.
cycling: Pay the cycling cost and discard this card to draw a card.
kicker: You may pay an extra cost as you cast this spell to get a bonus effect.
mentor: Whenever this creature attacks, put a +1/+1 counter on another attacking creature with lesser power.
afflict: Whenever this creature becomes blocked, the defending player loses that much life.
exalted: Whenever a creature you control attacks alone, that creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn for each instance of exalted.
annihilator: Whenever this creature attacks, the defending player sacrifices that many of their permanents.
infect: This deals damage to creatures as -1/-1 counters and to players as poison counters (10 poison counters lose the game).
absorb: If a source would deal damage to this creature, prevent that many points of that damage.
regenerate: The next time this would be destroyed this turn, instead tap it, remove it from combat, and heal all damage on it.
tap symbol: The {T} symbol in a cost means you must tap (turn sideways) the permanent to use that ability. A tapped permanent can't be tapped again until it untaps.
mana cost: The symbols in the top-right corner are what you pay to cast the card. A number like {2} means two mana of any color; a colored symbol like {W}, {U}, {B}, {R}, or {G} means one mana of that specific color (white, blue, black, red, green).
summoning sickness: A creature can't attack or use abilities with the {T} (tap) symbol until you've controlled it continuously since the start of your most recent turn — unless it has haste.
counter (spell): To 'counter' a spell means to stop it from happening; the countered spell does nothing and goes to its owner's graveyard.
counter (marker): A +1/+1 counter is a small marker placed on a creature that permanently raises its power and toughness by 1 each while it's there. Other counters (like -1/-1 or loyalty) work similarly.
sacrifice: To sacrifice a permanent is to move one you control to the graveyard. Because you chose to, it can't be stopped by 'can't be destroyed' effects.
exile: To exile a card is to set it aside out of the game. Exiled cards don't go to the graveyard and usually can't be gotten back unless an effect says so.
tokens: A token is a creature or object created by a spell or ability that isn't a real card. If it ever leaves the battlefield, it disappears.
legendary: You can only control one permanent with a given legendary name at a time. If you get a second, you choose one to keep and put the rest into the graveyard.
